page: Microsoft Azure E4ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Eadv6 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 236 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with the stress-ng single-core CPU test scoring 3080.18 and the Geekbench single-core test scoring 2103.0, both placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is average, as shown by a Geekbench multi-core score of 4846.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 6152.26. However, memory bandwidth benchmarks indicate weaknesses, with read-only small block and large block bandwidth falling into the bottom 25%. Database operations also show lower performance, with Passmark database operations scoring 2048.02, placing in the bottom 25%.

Given its high memory density and dedicated AMD EPYC processor, this instance provides a cost-efficient profile for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. The bundled 236 GB NVMe SSD provides fast local scratch space, making it suitable for memory-intensive applications, caching layers, and lightweight web serving. However, due to weak multi-threaded decompression and poor medium-model LLM inference speeds, it is less suitable for heavy parallel computing, software compilation, or complex AI inference tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure E4ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM. This configuration delivers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, supported by a bundled 236 GB NVMe SSD. Benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores ranking in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance and memory read bandwidth are relatively weak, with Passmark database operations and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falling into the bottom 25%. This server is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-heavy, single-threaded, or moderately threaded workloads such as caching, static web serving, and memory-bound applications, though it is constrained in highly parallelized computing and database-heavy operations.
